summary: Konan Naito (1866–1934) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Akita Normal School (~1880–1885) and held a post at Kyoto University (~1907–1926), where he taught Taichiro Kobayashi.
Konchok Drakpa studied under Thubten Chökyi Dorje and Patrul Rinpoche, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held an attested post at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.
Konchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Konchok Yeshe Ozer studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Konrad Klaus (born 1956) works in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn (~1980–1985), held Vertretungsprofessor posts at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001), and succeeded Claus Vogel in 2001.
Kosai Fukushima (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Paul L. Swanson. At Otani University, he was attested as Dean of Students in 1985 and professor in 1992.

Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) worked in history/archaeology, sinology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), he held posts there (~1909–1913) and at Kyoto University (~1913–1938), teaching Taichiro Kobayashi and Seiichi Mizuno.

Kosei Ishii (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa, and later held positions at Waseda, Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and Komazawa University (2006–2021).

Kosei Tada (1938–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies and studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1969). He held a post at Taisho University (~1971–2009) and served as board chairman of the Society for the Study of Buddhist Culture (attested 2004).

Kosen Imakita (1816–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shokoku-ji and Sōgen-ji under figures including Shoen Daisetsu and Gisan Zenkai. He served as abbot of Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892).
Koshin Suzuki (born 1959) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held an attested researcher post from 1995 to 1998.

Koshiro Tamaki (1915–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at Toyo University (1954), the University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Kawamura (born 1924) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura, later serving at Toyo University (~1957–1995), Minobusan, Hamamatsu, and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Kosho Mizutani (1928–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Ryukoku University (~1952–1956) and Bukkyo University. He served as professor and president of Bukkyo University (~1979–1989) and chaired the boards of Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen and Tokai Gakuen.
Kosho Murakami (born 1934) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Kodo Sawaki and Hideki Yukawa.
Koshu Itabashi (1927–2020) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sendai Daiichi High School, the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy, and Tohoku University (~1949–1953) under Teruji Ishizu.

Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and was attested at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra in 2001.

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and under doctoral supervisors Shoson Miyamoto and Hajime Nakamura. He served at Hokkaido University (~1969–1986), Osaka University, and Sapporo Otani Junior College.
Kotetsu Yoshida (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2014 as professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies.
